reason: Two things moved that the reasoning does not price. First, `because` and `given` are built around Together AI as the anchor of the tier at $8.3B, but bridge validation.cca768b345fbec01 (2026-07-17) records Fireworks AI at a $17.5B valuation, past $1B ARR and 40 trillion tokens a day -- Fireworks is now roughly twice Together's mark, so the named anchor whose capital needs are supposed to force the listing is no longer the company the reasoning names. Second, and new since the 2026-07-19 pass judged this fresh: the 2026-07-25 report carries Stripe opening talks to buy OpenRouter near $10B. That is an alternative liquidity path materialising inside the open-model inference layer -- trade sale to a payments incumbent rather than a public listing -- which is a live competing resolution to the `so_that` clause ('one open-model inference neocloud takes a disclosed public-listing step'). It went unattached as a bridge, so the reasoning is the right place to absorb it. Recommend reframing `because`/`given` around the tier rather than around Together specifically, and having `so_that` acknowledge M&A as the rival exit route. Confidence held below 0.7 because both `because` and `given` remain literally true as history and the window (2027-10-01..2027-12-31) is long; this is a framing-currency problem, not a falsification.
